marie: Quick share — apples-to-apples replay vs synthetic for streaming/non-streaming on rendu-v2 kernel selection + batching knobs.
marie: TL;DR: streaming improves p50/p95 for long outputs when KV cache hit rate >= 80% and chunk-size <= 128 tokens. non-streaming (batched) gives better tokens/sec and cost efficiency at steady high QPS.
marie: I pushed raw logs and dashboards to /bench/reports/180432 — see graphs: throughput_vs_qps.png, latency_cdf_streaming_vs_batch.png

anil: Nice. What were the input distributions? prompt len / gen len?
marie: We replayed 12k real requests from prod (avg prompt 64 tokens, gen 256) and also ran synthetic rps sweeps with fixed prompt/gen shapes.
marie: Repro commands:
```
# replay harness
./bench/replay --trace=prod-180421.json --mode=streaming --chunk-size=64 --kernel=auto --batch-max=32
# synthetic ramp
./bench/synth --qps 200 --seq-in 64 --seq-out 256 --mode=batched --kernel=fast-matmul
```

kate: Did you pin kernel versions? last time auto picked sgemm on 8bit and we saw KV stray evictions.
marie: Yes pinned kernels in the final runs: rendu-v2: kernel=matmul-fused-v3 for seq<=128, kernel=split-attn for longer. The auto run used heuristics which flipped to sgemm for some sequences.

jeff: How did you measure KV cache behavior? hit/evict metrics?
marie: We enriched traces with KV.metrics -> {hit_ratio, evicted_keys, avg_kv_read_ms}
marie: Example: streaming run at 150 qps: hit_ratio=0.84, evicted_keys=120, avg_kv_read_ms=0.9ms; batch run same qps: hit_ratio=0.57, evicted_keys=430, avg_kv_read_ms=2.8ms

perf-bot: auto-bench finished: streaming p50=89ms p95=412ms tokens/s=72 cost_per_1M= $14.2
perf-bot: auto-bench finished: batch p50=121ms p95=300ms tokens/s=118 cost_per_1M= $9.8

sylvia: Interesting — streaming lower p50 but p95 worse sometimes. Any backpressure events in client readloop?
marie: We instrumented readloop latency and saw backpressure spikes when chunking at 256: client loop stalled on partial frames, causing server queues to grow.
marie: Shorter chunks (<=128) reduced RT tail and prevented client-side stalls.

anil: Did you try adaptive batching heuristics? e.g., batch until either N or timeout T.
marie: Yep. Adaptive with N=16 or T=30ms performed best for mixed traffic. We also tried batching by sequence length buckets.
marie: Config snippet:
```
batching:
  max_batch: 32
  timeout_ms: 30
  length_buckets: [64,128,256,512]
```

jeff: Any regressions compared to last week's kernel-switch PR?
sylvia: We saw a small regen: kernel selector added fallback that increased KV reads for ~5% of traces -> extra latency ~8-12ms per request.
marie: Filed issue #8423. PR to tighten fallback thresholds forthcoming.

devops-bot: Alert - bench-run-180432 used 3% more mem on gpus during batch mode; tracked as perf-ci:mem-increase-180432

kate: Action items?
marie: 1) Rerun with fixed kernel pins + both chunk sizes (64/128) across the full replay set.
marie: 2) Run synthetic wide qps sweep with adaptive batching on/off.
marie: 3) Add kv eviction histo to dashboards and alert if evict_rate > 0.1 per 1k reqs.

anil: I'll take (1). jeff will own (2). sylvia will own (3).

jeff: ack, starting synth sweeps now. posting results in this thread.
marie: thanks all :thumbsup:
